answer: A UDP Flood attack works by an adversary sending a high volume of UDP packets to a target, aiming to consume the available network bandwidth and deny legitimate users access to the service. This type of attack can overwhelm not only the target's network resources but also the resources of firewalls, which may open ports for each UDP connection. Consequently, the high packet nature of a UDP flood can exhaust the connection state resources allocated by the firewall. UDP Flood attacks can specifically target services such as DNS or VoIP, further impacting their availability and functionality [Source 1].
